🇲🇽⛏️ <u>Mexico's Mining Output Value Jumps 21% to 379 Billion Pesos</u>

The value of Mexico's mining and metallurgical production hit 379.3 billion pesos in 2025, up 21.2% from 2024, according to the mining chamber Camimex. Gold made up 33.4% of it, copper 24.6% and silver 24.3%. Mining exports reached $30.6 billion, up 19.8%. Physical volume barely moved: the jump came from metal prices, and Camimex blames slow permit renewals for flat output.

🇲🇽📊 <u>INEGI: The Economy Grew in 28 of Mexico's 32 States</u>

INEGI's state-level activity index for the second quarter of 2026 shows growth in 28 states. San Luis Potosí and Veracruz led with 3.6% quarterly growth each, followed by Jalisco at 3.2%. National GDP rose 1.4% in the same quarter, and only four states contracted. (El Economista)

🇲🇽🏔️ <u>Fonatur Puts 20 Million Pesos Into Oaxaca's Community-Run Tourism</u>

The Pueblos Mancomunados are eight Zapotec communities in the Sierra Norte of Oaxaca. Their ecotourism is owned and run by the communities themselves, with no hotel chain and no megaproject. Mexico's tourism development fund has transferred 20 million pesos to them, and the first equipment is going into San Miguel Amatlán and Santa Catarina Lachatao. The money will restore public spaces, infrastructure and heritage sites. Fonatur ranks the network among the country's first three priority community-tourism destinations.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Pablo Gómez: In 2015, the INE Counted More Than 100% of Polling Stations</u>

At Thursday's mañanera, Pablo Gómez, then a legislative adviser at the INE, recalled the 2015 midterm district count. The results system had been bought without a tender and was overseen by a "technical committee" of the contractors' friends, and at one point it showed more than 100% of polling stations counted. "They say we're a magical country, but this is beyond magic." He said Lorenzo Córdova, then INE president, "never showed up to explain anything."

🇲🇽⚡ <u>CFE Posts Its Sixth Straight Quarter Above a 30% Margin</u>

The CFE that the neoliberals wanted to shrink until private generators took over reported 164.1 billion pesos in EBITDA for January-September 2026, a 31.7% margin. It sold 3.4% more energy while spending 6.3% less on fuel. Cash on hand rose 30% to 190.2 billion pesos, and leverage fell from 58.6% to 52.2% in a year.

🇲🇽🎓 <u>For the First Time, the IPN's Own Community Helps Pick Its Director</u>

For decades, the director of Mexico's Instituto Politécnico Nacional was simply appointed from above. This time students, teachers and staff vote first. Candidates register Nov 2-6, and electronic voting across all three sectors runs Nov 25-27. Two shortlists, three women and three men, go in a sealed envelope to President Sheinbaum on December 1.

🇲🇽🍎 <u>Junk Food Is Out of Mexico's Schools: One Year In</u>

A year after the ban took effect, Education Secretary Mario Delgado told lawmakers that junk food is gone from Mexico's basic-education schools. The industry is still fighting it with more than 139 amparo suits. "We expelled junk food from basic-education schools in a single year, and we will keep fighting the big corporations in court so these products don't come back."

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Mexico's Legal Diesel Market Posts Its Biggest Jump in a Decade</u>

Mexico's apparent diesel consumption rose 22.2% from January to August, to a record 459.2 thousand barrels a day, according to Sener figures reported by El Economista. The jump coincides with the crackdown on fuel smuggling that began with the seizure of the tanker Challenge Procyon in Tampico in March 2025. Diesel that used to come in mislabeled as lubricant now shows up in the legal market.

Pemex diesel sales grew 18.4% to 320.1 thousand barrels a day, and the share of imports fell from 46.7% to 39.3%.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>UN Adopts Mexico's Resolution Against Arms Trafficking</u>

At the Palermo Convention conference in Vienna, member states unanimously adopted a resolution presented by Mexico and Honduras against illicit firearms trafficking, the Foreign Ministry (SRE) reported. It targets the corruption that lets criminal groups make and move weapons. It also urges governments to trace recovered guns and use that data to map trafficking networks.

Sheinbaum has said 75% of the weapons in Mexico come from the United States. Since October 2024, Mexican forces have seized 36,300 illegal firearms.

🇲🇽🕊️ <u>"Hasta Siempre, Ingeniero": Mexico's Government Honors Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas</u>

The government opened Thursday's morning press conference with a farewell to Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas. Sheinbaum called it a deeply felt loss and pointed to his idea of democracy: one "that comes from below, not the democracy of the elites."

Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez said the homage also belongs "to those who suffered persecution by an authoritarian regime and to those who lost their lives winning freedoms."
